claims.claim: The highest-risk flaw is the convergence rule: it trusts self-reported metadata (`agreed_with_peer` coverage plus empty `disagreed_with_peer`) instead of independently checking whether substantive disagreements were actually resolved, so polite agents can false-converge.

Required `evidence_path` fields improve syntax, not truthfulness: the shipped deliberation path never verifies that a cited file/line exists or supports the claim, so agents can satisfy the schema with bogus citations and still pass both unit tests and live strict-mode smoke tests.

The current two-agent topology already has a bigger blind spot than missing a third agent: round 1 is not truly independent, because `agent_b` runs after `agent_a` and can see `agent_a`'s first position before forming its own. I would fix true independent first-pass generation before adding agent 3.

If `max_rounds` grows past 5, the first structural failure is convergence drift plus synthesis-history scaling, not per-turn prompt bloat: agent turns only see `peer_latest` and `own_prior`, but the workflow keeps appending full `position_history` and dumps the whole chronology into synthesis, while convergence only inspects the latest claim IDs.

Asymmetric duet plus symmetric deliberation is a reasonable top-level partition; the missing piece is not a third user-facing workflow but a reusable verifier/adjudicator stage that both patterns can call when they need grounded resolution rather than self-reported agreement.

evidence.content_snippet: "converged" if round >= 2 and every agent's latest position has an empty `disagreed_with_peer` AND covers every claim ID the peer last emitted in `agreed_with_peer`.
evidence.label: Convergence Rule Is Mechanical

evidence.content_snippet: "Reference peer claims by their claim_id when acknowledging or disagreeing." ... "Return a Position JSON object ..."
evidence.label: Prompt Only Demands Claim-ID Referencing

evidence.content_snippet: "Neither has peer context on its own first call ... agent_b's first prompt may have agent_a's round-1 position."
evidence.label: Round-1 Independence Is Already Compromised

evidence.content_snippet: The tests only assert that missing `evidence_path` raises `ValidationError` for `PositionClaim` and `DisagreementAtom`.
evidence.label: Evidence Path Is Presence-Checked, Not Verified

evidence.content_snippet: "minimum live-LLM round-trip ... asserts the call returns without a schema-validation error."
evidence.label: Live Smoke Tests Only Prove Provider Schema Acceptance

evidence.content_snippet: "list every cited file:line ... you could not open or whose claimed content you could not confirm."
evidence.label: Plan-Doc Review Already Has Citation-Verification Vocabulary

evidence.content_snippet: "Deliberation v1 requires exactly 2 agents ... N-agent (≥3) is a future extension."
evidence.label: Builder Hard-Locks V1 To Exactly Two Agents

open_questions: Does `llm_client` core enforce a cumulative spend cap across all calls sharing one `trace_id`, or does the workflow layer's repeated reuse of the same `max_budget` rely entirely on lower-layer behavior?
Would a third agent still add net signal after fixing round-1 independence and adding audited claim resolution, or would it mostly add cost and more paths to bogus agreement metadata?

Should claim identity become chassis-owned across rounds (stable IDs / lineage) rather than agent-authored free text, to prevent renamed or silently dropped claims from disappearing out of the convergence check?
reviewer_summary: Ranking by leverage: (1) replace self-reported convergence with an evidence-audited adjudication ledger, (2) verify citations rather than only requiring `evidence_path` strings, (3) fix true round-1 independence before expanding topology, (4) then address longer-run history/claim-drift scaling. The single highest-priority next improvement is an adjudicator/verifier stage that checks cited evidence and emits per-claim statuses such as supported/refuted/unverified; convergence should depend on that ledger instead of `agreed_with_peer`/`disagreed_with_peer`. That one change directly attacks the two most dangerous shipped failure modes: polite false convergence and bogus groundedness.
